name: Moroni
subtitle: Moroni, capital of Comoros: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 121,236 people live in Moroni Bambao (the commune of Moroni) (counted 2017).

Moroni became the administrative capital of the Comoros; sources differ on the year the colonial capital moved there (1958 per EBSCO's full article, 1962 per Library of Congress) and EBSCO also ties it to independence in 1975.
Protectorate treaties were signed with the rulers of Njazidja, Nzwani and Mwali in 1886; the islands joined France's Madagascar colony in 1908 and the last sultan abdicated in 1912.

parts.text: Moroni became the administrative capital of the Comoros; sources differ on the year the colonial capital moved there (1958 per EBSCO's full article, 1962 per Library of Congress) and EBSCO also ties it to independence in 1975.
Protectorate treaties were signed with the rulers of Njazidja, Nzwani and Mwali in 1886; the islands joined France's Madagascar colony in 1908 and the last sultan abdicated in 1912.

Independence was declared on 6 July 1975 by the Comorian government for all the islands including Mayotte (Mahore); the Mayotte status remains disputed, with the Comorian position stated in UN debates.
Moroni was a capital of a pre-colonial sultanate: the 1892 French protectorate treaty names Moroni as capital of the Bambao sultanate and was signed in Moroni roadstead on 6 January 1892.
Moroni is described as a centre of Islamic culture and ocean trade, and one of the main ports of the islands.

blocks.prompt: About how many people do you think live in Moroni Bambao (the commune of Moroni)?

parts.text: 121,236 in 2017, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Census 2017 (RGPH-2017) count for the administrative subdivision 'Moroni Bambao' on Ngazidja (61,867 male, 59,369 female).

items.text: The Old Friday Mosque in Moroni is built, according to Mayotte Hebdo's report on the medina inscription.
AFP describes Moroni's medina as 14th-century, including the Friday Mosque with its green minaret.
French protectorate treaties are signed with the rulers of the three islands including Njazidja (Grande Comore).
A protectorate treaty for Grande Comore, naming Moroni as capital of Bambao, is signed in Moroni roadstead aboard the Eure.
The last sultan abdicates and a colonial administration takes over the islands.
The colonial capital moves from Dzaoudzi (Mayotte) to Moroni. Sources conflict on the year: Library of Congress 1962, EBSCO 1958.
The Comoros declares independence; Moroni becomes the capital of the new state.
Six medinas of the Comoros, including Moroni's, are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list (reported by AFP and RFI).
